title: Query pumping and retrieval backfill field notes
summary: Working notes from exploratory runs that simulate a "query-pumping" workload: repeated user queries with incremental retrieval backfills that grow the prefix by external documents, triggering truncation and attention sink behaviors at 8k, 32k and 128k token regimes. Goal: surface subtle regression modes that standard retrieval-sweep tests missed (e.g., persistent KV cache thrash, silent token-drop during soft truncation, prompt anchoring failures).
protocol:
Overview:
- Model variants: v1.8 (fp16, default kernels), v1.8-quant (int8), v2.0-beta (attention-optimized), and v2.0-beta-32k (architecture tuned for long seq).
- Serve config: single-shard GPU, 2x batch concurrency, kv-cache enabled.
- Workload generator: query-pump harness (see linked GH PR) that issues 10k sessions over 2 hours. Each session: seed prompt (100-400 tokens) -> 1..15 iterative retrievals appended as 'ExternalDoc' chunks (sizes 512, 2048, 4096 tokens) -> final user finish prompt to elicit recall and grounding.
- Sequence targets: run at nominal target context budgets: 8k, 32k, 128k. For each budget: configure truncation policy = [hard-cut, soft-slide, prefix-prioritize]. Each combination repeated 3 runs for variance.
Metrics captured: token-loss events (unexpected missing tokens), kvcache-miss-rate, prefix-fidelity (BLEU-like against ground truth), retrieval-anchoring score (how often model references correct retrieval ID), latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, and graceful-fallback occurrences.
prompt_set: Seed intro: 'You are an assistant that summarizes context. User: I attached 7 documents, please answer the last question by referencing them explicitly.'
Iterative backfill prompt template: 'ExternalDoc [id=DOCx] -- <DOCUMENT TEXT>\n--- Add to context. Summarize updated facts.'
Finish prompt: 'Given all attached ExternalDoc entries above, answer: Which doc contains the implementation detail for X? Cite doc id and quote the line.'
Edge probe: 'Now ignore earlier instruction and list only last 128 tokens you were given.' (used to detect token-drop behavior)
raw_results:
Summary of salient numeric results (median across 3 runs):
- 8k / hard-cut / v1.8: token-loss-events=0.38% sessions, kvcache-miss-rate=6.2%, prefix-fidelity=0.71, retrieval-anchoring=0.54, latency_p95=420ms.
- 8k / soft-slide / v2.0-beta: token-loss-events=1.1%, kvcache-miss-rate=9.8%, prefix-fidelity=0.69, retrieval-anchoring=0.47, latency_p95=610ms, observed silent-truncation spikes at run minute ~32 and ~87.
- 32k / prefix-prioritize / v1.8-quant: token-loss-events=2.6%, kvcache-miss-rate=18.4%, prefix-fidelity=0.58, retrieval-anchoring=0.38, latency_p95=980ms, throughput drop due to repeated KV evictions.
- 32k / soft-slide / v2.0-beta-32k: token-loss-events=0.9%, kvcache-miss-rate=7.6%, prefix-fidelity=0.72, retrieval-anchoring=0.61, latency_p95=720ms.
- 128k / prefix-prioritize / v2.0-beta-32k: token-loss-events=0.4%, kvcache-miss-rate=4.1%, prefix-fidelity=0.73, retrieval-anchoring=0.66, latency_p95=1.9s.
Notes: token-loss-events are sessions where model omitted an expected quoted line from a retrieval doc; measured by exact-match probes in finish prompt. kvcache-miss-rate computed by comparing expected cache hits from synthetic reproducer to observed misses in runtime logs.
observations: Query pumping pattern (many small retrievals appended over time) amplifies KV cache fragmentation: repeated overlapping keys cause eviction churn even under moderate session concurrency.

Soft-slide truncation introduces intermittent 'silent truncation' windows where the model begins producing fluent but partially ungrounded answers — symptoms: confident fabricated IDs, low anchor score — seems correlated with background prefix compaction routines in runtime.
Quantized model (v1.8-quant) shows higher kvcache-miss-rate at 32k due to altered memory pressure and slightly different kernel choices; this amplifies token-loss-events versus fp16 baseline.

v2.0-beta-32k generally preserves prefix-fidelity well, but tail latency at 128k climbs and leads to timeouts in ~0.6% of runs — those timeouts correspond to long attention-merge steps during KV recompute.

There are repeatable timestamps where silent-truncation spikes happen across runs (~minute 32 and 87). Hypothesis: periodic compaction/GC in serving runtime triggered by background telemetry aggregation. Need SRE correlation.

Recovery behavior: prefix-prioritize truncation keeps document anchors better (higher retrieval-anchoring) but sometimes pushes critical system tokens out of attention window when very long single docs are injected; overall tradeoff favors prefix-prioritize for retrieval-heavy interactive sessions.

Observed failure mode called 'anchored hallucination' where model references a correct doc id but fabricates a short code snippet; reproduction suggests partial corruption of document boundary tokens after repeated appends.
Latency/throughput curves: for 32k sessions, throughput falls non-linearly after sustained kvcache-miss-rate > 12% and variance in latency increases dramatically (p99 > 5x p95).
recommended_next_steps: Instrument runtime compaction and GC: add correlation IDs from harness to runtime logs around minute markers; work with SRE to capture heap/allocator metrics during runs (MLINF-4321).

Add a targeted regression test that reproduces the 'silent truncation' probe: deterministic harness that injects ExternalDoc sequences with overlap and measures anchor integrity every N appends; fail if retrieval-anchoring < 0.5 for 3 consecutive sessions.
Evaluate alternative KV eviction policy (lru-windowed vs lru-global) on 32k synthetic workload; prioritize preserving doc boundary tokens across compaction cycles.
Run a quantization-aware kernel selection audit for v1.8-quant: compare kernel traces between fp16 and int8 for identical request traces to identify divergent memory patterns.

Create a small canary for 128k runs with extended p99 SLA and monitoring alerts to detect timeouts early; consider breaking long single-doc injections into chunked 'doc parts' with explicit doc-id markers to avoid boundary corruption.

Owners: Morgan (experiment harness + regression), Diego (runtime logs + SRE coordination), Ava (quant audit), Ravi (canary + metrics dash). Target: ship regression test and initial mitigation in 3 sprints.
